abstract: Innate immune pathways are therapeutic targets of prime importance, both for antiviral and neurodegenerative therapies. The Zika virus is highly evolved to manipulate these same pathways so expertly that half of infections go unnoticed. While the direct inhibition of immune effectors by ZIKV nonstructural proteins is well characterized, second order effects on immune responsive cellular functions are less understood. We induced the innate antiviral response in human microglia like cells, perturbed that response using 6 ZIKV nonstructural genes, and resolve systems level effects using scRNA-seq and hdWGCNA. We recapitulate known ZIKV bioactivity and identify specific suppression of the PA28 immunoproteasome by NS2B, demonstrating how ZIKV can shape tissue level neuroinflammation.
